title: Timers in Function Block Diagram: an off-delay light and an on-delay filter
summary: Wire a TOF block to keep a light on after a button is released, and a TON block to ignore a sensor blip that is too short.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence with one 10 ms task; they do not establish electrical debounce, sensor response, target timing, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Keep an output ON for a fixed time after its input drops, with a TOF block whose PT input is wired to a TIME constant.
Ignore an input that is ON for less than a fixed time, with a TON block, and say which timer delays the start and which one delays the end.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/Delays.fbd.json Button is wired straight to Light and Sensor straight to Confirmed. Light must stay ON for {{t:300}} ms after Button is released. Confirmed must turn ON only after Sensor has stayed ON for {{t:200}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which timer block keeps an output on and which one waits before turning it on.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: The scenario presses Button at {{t:100}} ms and releases it at {{t:300}} ms. Sensor blips ON from {{t:100}} ms to {{t:140}} ms and is ON again from {{t:500}} ms to {{t:900}} ms. Predict Light and Confirmed at {{t:200}}, {{t:450}}, {{t:650}}, and {{t:800}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:Delays.Light=true,Delays.Confirmed=false@200|Light ON, Confirmed OFF}} at {{t:200}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=true,Delays.Confirmed=false@450|Light ON, Confirmed OFF}} at {{t:450}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=false,Delays.Confirmed=false@650|both OFF}} at {{t:650}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=false,Delays.Confirmed=true@800|Confirmed ON, Light OFF}} at {{t:800}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this flaw of the starting diagram, save it, then press Check: The starting diagram wires the inputs straight to the outputs, so Light is already OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed turns ON for the {{t:100}} ms blip. Place a TOF block named HoldTimer, wire Button to its IN and a TIME constant T#300ms to its PT, and wire its Q to Light in place of the wire from Button. Do the same with a TON block named FilterTimer, Sensor and T#200ms for Confirmed. Save the file.
stages.checkpoint: Both timer blocks are in the diagram and each output is wired to its timer's Q.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named Delays and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Follow Light and Confirmed in the trace: the short blip never turns Confirmed ON, Light is still ON at {{t:450}} ms although Button went OFF at {{t:300}} ms, and Confirmed rises about {{t:200}} ms after Sensor came back at {{t:500}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: Light falls about {{t:300}} ms after Button, and Confirmed rises about {{t:200}} ms after the second Sensor pulse.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Swap the two timer blocks in your head: what would a TON on Button and a TOF on Sensor do with this scenario?
stages.checkpoint: TON delays the start and TOF delays the end; each answers a different question about a signal.

hints.text: TOF keeps its Q ON for the preset time after IN falls, and TON raises Q only after IN has been ON for the preset time.

Place a TOF block named HoldTimer with Button on IN and the constant T#300ms on PT, and its Q on Light. Place a TON block named FilterTimer with Sensor on IN and the constant T#200ms on PT, and its Q on Confirmed.

faultCases: The starting diagram wires the inputs straight to the outputs, so Light is already OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed turns ON for the {{t:100}} ms blip.
